narrative:
The model estimated a 68% chance that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning that if similar applicants were assessed, roughly seven in ten would be expected to have repayment problems. Because that risk exceeds the lender’s threshold, your application was denied.

The strongest factor was your credit history rating. Your category—all paid at bank—is unusually rare among approved applicants, at only about 3%, and it pushed the decision toward bad credit more than any other factor. The second most important factor was your checking account status: a balance of 0–200 DM is less common among approved applicants than having no checking account or an unknown status, and it also increased the perceived risk. The third factor was the loan purpose. A new car loan was not the most common approved purpose and it added to the risk assessment, though less strongly than your credit history and checking account status. All three top factors pushed toward denial rather than toward approval.

To improve your next application, focus on strengthening your checking account balance and building a more typical, consistent credit record. Ask the lender whether there are specific steps you can take, consider a smaller or secured loan, and reapply once your financial profile is stronger.
